title: Calibration of Agentic Risk Assessment: Do Agents Correctly Estimate the Risk Level of Their Own Actions?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If agents are systematically miscalibrated in risk assessment, it undermines any safety protocol relying on self-monitoring. The reversible vs irreversible dimension is practically important. Clear path from finding to intervention (calibration training).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Eliciting risk scores from an agent via prompting is straightforward. Comparing against human annotations is standard methodology. The main challenge is creating 100 actions with well-calibrated human risk ratings, but this is conceptual work rather than engineering complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: calibration plot of self-assessed vs human-assessed risk. However, creating and annotating 100 actions with reliable human risk scores is time-intensive. Could be scoped to 30-40 actions for a pilot study.
